title: [CI] Run independent milan_dp simulation legs in a bounded pool
body:
[A10] Current correction: A179 Codex implements the [explicit host-tool boundary decision](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/517#issuecomment-5781783857); the existing acceptance and R245/R246 review bar are unchanged.

[A10] Current scheduling: A178 Codex resumes after the published shared-header decision; R245 internal Codex and R246 external Opus are reserved. Earlier role/scheduling paragraphs below are historical.

[A10] Focused follow-up to #270's CI optimization work, using #445's landed timing instrumentation and preserving #444's dedicated suite worker. No new generic cache or sharding lane is proposed.

## Objective and evidence

Shorten the mandatory `milan_dp` suite by running its independent, already-built ordinary simulation legs in a bounded pool. Preserve the models, tests, results and complete merge bar.

At source `1496558d82cf35fc98dda0e781b2a1be643c301a`, [hosted run 35739098185](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/actions/runs/35739098185) spends 1999 seconds in the dedicated `milan_dp` worker; the next-longest Verilator worker takes 723 seconds. The render mutation driver occupies 563.630 seconds, including 131.120 seconds of mutant builds and 432.394 seconds of simulations. The remaining suite time is not fully attributed, so these figures do not claim that all remaining time is simulation.

[Immutable measured log, 23 phase records, artifact identity and decision](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/tree/8326a88dc21a34bbcd0af7c0c0b6ecd0204704f4/review-evidence/478-r1/throughput-analysis). The artifact's TARGET_SHA was verified. The last two completed all-workflow local replicas took 4500.957 and 4534.164 seconds; these distinct heads are context, not a controlled optimization benchmark.

## Authority and entry points

- REQUIREMENTS REQ-VER-01/02/04; CONTRIBUTING sections 2/3; AGENTS review/merge contract.
- `docs/testing/CI_WORKFLOWS.md`, `scripts/run_all_suites.sh`, `scripts/suite_tally.py`.
- `tb/verilator/milan_dp/Makefile`, especially the ten ordinary executable calls at the tail of `run`.
- The selected `sim_main.cpp`/`sim_nxn.cpp`/`sim_prune.cpp`/`sim_aclk.cpp` harnesses, `render_mutants.py` and the suite README; confirm exact source names from Makefile variables.
- #386's render-law controls, #445's observation contract and #444's dedicated worker/deadline decision.

## Settled scope

Introduce a small suite-local runner for exactly the ten ordinary simulation commands already present after the model builds. Default to two concurrent children; retain one-worker mode for comparison/reproduction. Keep existing build recipes, gPTP prerequisite runs and the render mutation driver in their existing execution phases. Run the mutation driver only after all ordinary legs succeed. Preserve all executable arguments, model parameters, seeds, clocks, timers, cycle windows, assertions, named checks, mutation controls and suite ownership.

Capture each child separately and emit its complete output in the existing deterministic order. An unsuccessful or missing child cannot become a passing suite. Bound concurrency even under a larger inherited make job count. Cancellation must terminate and reap every owned child/process group, retain attributable partial logs, and leave no simulation running after the parent exits.

The [shared-header decision](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/517#issuecomment-5780545051) supersedes the original read-only generated-input premise: serialize all five sim_nxn legs as one exclusive group in their original relative order, since the existing builder also rewrites repository-relative shape headers. Other audited independent legs may overlap that group within the total two-child limit. Preserve generator arguments and writes, verify grouped exclusion with fault-sensitive controls, and record tracked-header integrity before/after benchmarks. `sim_nxn` uses unique temporary image directories, but `MILAN_COUNTER_FRAME_OUT` selects a shared writable file. When that variable is present, use the original sequential order for the whole ordinary-leg set, preserving its current final-output semantics. If another shared mutable dependency is found, publish the evidence before proceeding; do not silently parallelize it.

PP (protocol processor) and gPTP processor models, pins and ownership remain unchanged. No production RTL/firmware edits, scenario shortening, weakened failure/timeout handling, result caching, workflow reshuffling, act concurrency change, hardware work or budget increase.

## Acceptance and validation

1. Inventory every selected command and demonstrate that the sequential and pooled modes execute each exactly once with identical arguments and input identities. Builds, gPTP prerequisites and render controls remain included in the default suite.
2. At the same clean commit and pinned Verilator 5.050, compare sequential versus two-worker output and per-leg verdict/check totals. Report same-host full-suite cold/warm timings separately, actual concurrency and peak resource use. The full suite must measurably improve; publish actual gains and limitations, not a promised percentage. If it does not improve, revise the public decision before promotion.
3. Failure-sensitive runner tests cover a failing child, a crash, a missing executable, delayed/out-of-order completion, preserved complete logs, the two-child ceiling, invalid worker counts, interruption with descendants, and no surviving owned processes. The optional frame-dump path must select the original sequential behavior and preserve its outcome.
4. The complete real `milan_dp` suite and unchanged render mutation driver pass. `suite_tally.py --verdict` records the same real test counts, with no telemetry counted as tests. Existing phase-observation tests and relevant documentation/idiom/evidence gates pass without ratchet growth.
5. Run and record the full required local banks, trusted act replica, exact-head hosted gates, independent internal/external reviews across all five lenses, current merge candidate and post-merge containment. Compare hosted dedicated-worker timing with the attributable baseline; do not use a different tool/version or a smaller test inventory as speedup evidence.

## Roles, readiness and lane conflicts

Ready: the first optimization and shared-output policy above are selected. Reserved executor A173 Opus; cleared-context internal reviewer R245 Opus and external reviewer R246 Codex; manager A10. Start implementation only when the current sole author A160 on #504 finishes. Create its branch through `gh issue develop` from then-current dev. No active lane owns these simulation files. Any edits to shared workflow contracts require a separate public scope decision and wait for #504.

The initial merge queue remains #512, #372, #423, #504. This optimization follows those lanes; its implementation/review may overlap their validation once its own lane opens. #270 retains ownership of broader setup/cache/act-isolation proposals and their completed results.
